Mother of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, martyred at Sirhind.
Legendary Sikh woman warrior who led the 40 Sikhs back to the battlefield of Muktsar.
Venerated Sikh scholar and warrior who fought for the sanctity of the Golden Temple.
Great scholar and martyr who served multiple Gurus and was martyred at Lahore.
Sikh martyr who sacrificed his life to uphold the sanctity of his hair (Kesh).
Emblem of selfless service who provided water to all wounded in the battlefield.
Founder and first Maharaja of the Sikh Empire, known as Sher-e-Punjab.
Venerable figure who served the first six Sikh Gurus.
Great scholar and scribe of the original Adi Granth.
Lifelong companion of Guru Nanak Dev Ji and a master of the Rebab.
Prominent musician who served in the Guru's court.
Celebrated musician and contributor to the Guru Granth Sahib.

Sikh martyr broken on the wheel for his faith (1745).
Young Sikh martyr and son of Bhai Subeg Singh (1745).
The martyr who resembled Guru Gobind Singh Ji and stayed in the Chamkaur Haveli.
Revolutionary saint and poet whose hymns are extensively featured in the Sri Guru Granth Sahib.
Celebrated saint from Maharashtra whose hymns are enshrined in the Sri Guru Granth Sahib.
Revolutionary saint and social reformer who advocated for dignity and equality.
12th-century Sufi saint whose hymns are in Guru Granth Sahib.
Pioneer of the Bhakti movement who advocated for devotion regardless of caste.
Renowned poet from Bengal, author of Gita Govinda.
Saint from Maharashtra who emphasized internal purity.
Farmer-saint from Rajasthan who realized God through pure faith.
Devoted saint who represented the dignity of honest labor.
Royal figure who renounced his throne for spiritual devotion.
Sufi saint whose hymns reflect on the supreme value of the Divine Name.
Devout saint who demonstrated that no profession is a barrier to spiritual realization.
Dedicated devotee whose compositions reflect deep surrender to the Almighty.
Famous saint and poet immersed in the Divine Name.
Mystical saint whose deep spiritual insights are preserved in the Sikh scripture.
Most prominent among the 11 Bhatts in the Sri Guru Granth Sahib.
Bhatt poet who wrote in praise of Guru Amar Das Ji.
Bhatt poet who composed in praise of Guru Amar Das Ji and Guru Ram Das Ji.
Bhatt poet who described Guru Amar Das Ji as a true spiritual guide.
Bhatt poet who composed in praise of Guru Amar Das Ji and Guru Ram Das Ji.
Bhatt poet who composed Sawaiyas in praise of Guru Amar Das Ji.
Significant Bhatt poet known for his devotion to Guru Ram Das Ji.
Bhatt poet known for the use of the word 'Waheguru' in his hymns.
Prominent Bhatt poet in the Sikh scripture.
Bhatt poet who composed hymns in praise of Guru Ram Das Ji.
Bhatt poet who composed Sawaiyas in praise of Guru Arjan Dev Ji.
Consort of Guru Angad Dev Ji, pioneer of Guru Ka Langar, whose selfless seva is specifically praised in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.
Spiritual Mother of the Khalsa Panth (Mata Sahib Kaur), who added patashas (sugar crystals) into the Amrit during the first Amrit Sanchar in 1699.
Consort of Guru Gobind Singh Ji who guided the Sikh community from Delhi after 1708 and commissioned Bhai Mani Singh Ji to compile the Guru's works.
Devout early disciple and lifelong companion of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji on his historic travels (Udasis).
Devoted merchant who proclaimed 'Guru Ladho Re' (The Guru is Found!) from the rooftops of Baba Bakala, identifying Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.
Devout Sikh who heroically retrieved the headless sacred torso of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji in Delhi and cremated it by burning down his own home (Gurdwara Rakab Ganj Sahib).
Fearless Nihang leader who made the supreme sacrifice defending Sri Harmandir Sahib with 30 brave warriors against Ahmad Shah Durrani's invading army in 1764.
Daring Sikh warrior who, along with Bhai Mehtab Singh, rode into Amritsar in 1740 disguised as revenue collectors to eliminate Massa Ranghar for desecrating the Golden Temple.
Valiant warrior of Mirankot who entered Sri Harmandir Sahib to punish Massa Ranghar and was later martyred on the spiked wheel in Lahore in 1745.
Brave Sikh who challenged Mughal sovereignty in 1739 by setting up a toll post at Sarai Nurdin, declaring Khalsa sovereignty, and attained martyrdom along with Bhai Garja Singh.
Companion of Bhai Bota Singh who fought shoulder to shoulder against a Mughal detachment to demonstrate that the Khalsa was alive and undefeated.
Courageous Sikh woman who gathered the sacred bodies of the Sahibzadas and martyrs of Chamkaur Sahib under cover of night and performed their funeral rites, attaining martyrdom.
Supreme Commander of Dal Khalsa who led Sikhs through the Great Holocaust (Vadda Ghalughara), captured Lahore in 1761, liberated Delhi in 1783, and struck Sikh coins.
Renowned general, architect, and chief of the Ramgarhia Misl who fortified Ram Rauni and brought back the Mughal coronation slab from Delhi's Red Fort to the Ramgarhia Bunga in Amritsar.
Legendary Nihang supremo, fearless Jathedar of Sri Akal Takht Sahib, and commander whose unmatched valor secured pivotal victories for Maharaja Ranjit Singh at Multan, Kashmir, and Nowshera.
Legendary Commander-in-Chief of the Sikh Khalsa Army who conquered the Khyber Pass, subdued fierce Afghan tribes, built the Jamrud Fort, and stopped invasions from Central Asia.
Venerable Sikh general who took a sacred vow never to return defeated, leading an epic last charge clad in white robes at the Battle of Sobraon in 1846 during the First Anglo-Sikh War.
Youngest queen of Maharaja Ranjit Singh and Queen Regent of the Sikh Empire who mounted fierce anti-British resistance, famously described by the British as 'the Messalina of the Punjab'.
Heroic leader of the peaceful jatha during Saka Nankana Sahib in 1921, who was tied to a Jand tree and burnt alive while reciting Japji Sahib to liberate Guru Nanak's birthplace.
Daring and resolute leader of the Gurdwara Reform Movement who successfully liberated Sri Panja Sahib, Sri Nankana Sahib, and Sri Tarn Taran Sahib from corrupt mahants.

persons.nameRoman: Bhai Karam Singh Ji (Saka Panja Sahib)
persons.nameHindi: भाई करम सिंह जी (साका पंजा साहिब)
persons.shortBio: Martyr of Saka Panja Sahib (1922) who, along with Bhai Partap Singh, laid down his life on the railway tracks to halt a speeding train to feed starved Sikh freedom fighters.

persons.nameRoman: Bhai Partap Singh Ji (Saka Panja Sahib)
persons.nameHindi: भाई प्रताप सिंह जी (साका पंजा साहिब)
persons.shortBio: Revered Granthi and freedom hero who sat in deep prayer on the tracks at Panja Sahib railway station in 1922, giving his life to stop the train and serve langar to imprisoned Sikhs.
Visionary merchant and patriot who chartered the Japanese ship SS Komagata Maru in 1914 to challenge discriminatory Canadian immigration exclusion laws and fight for Indian independence.
Youthful mastermind of the Ghadar Party revolution who was hanged by the British at just 19 years of age in 1915; the foremost political and spiritual inspiration of Bhagat Singh.
Founding President of the Ghadar Party in the United States and Canada, who spent over 26 years in British colonial prisons fighting for the liberation of the motherland.
Fearless patriot who tracked and executed former Lieutenant Governor of Punjab Michael O'Dwyer in London in 1940 to avenge the brutal Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919.
National revolutionary icon whose intellectual depth, courage, and martyrdom in Lahore Central Jail in 1931 at age 23 energized India's freedom struggle.

'Betaj Badshah' (Uncrowned King) of the Sikhs, first President of the SGPC, and pioneer of the Keys Morcha whose victory was hailed by Mahatma Gandhi as the first decisive battle of Indian freedom won.
Paramount Sikh political and religious statesman of the 20th century who led the Shiromani Akali Dal, SGPC, and the Punjabi Suba Movement to safeguard Sikh political identity.
Venerated saint, educator, and visionary who revived Sikh education by establishing dozens of schools and colleges, and laid the foundation stone of Banaras Hindu University in 1914.
Scholar-saint holding degrees from Harvard University and Cambridge, appointed ambassador of Sikhi abroad by Sant Attar Singh, and founder of The Kalgidhar Trust and Baru Sahib.
Spiritual mystic, freedom fighter, and founder of the Akhand Kirtani Jatha who endured 16 years of harsh British imprisonment, inspiring countless with his spiritual memoirs (Jail Chithian).

persons.nameGurmukhi: ਸੰਤ ਜਰਨੈਲ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਖ਼ਾਲਸਾ ਭਿੰਡਰਾਂਵਾਲੇ
persons.nameRoman: Sant Jarnail Singh Ji Khalsa Bhindranwale
persons.nameHindi: संत जरनैल सिंह जी खालसा भिंडरांवाले
persons.shortBio: 14th Jathedar of Damdami Taksal whose magnetic preaching inspired hundreds of thousands into Amrit Sanchar and who championed the Anandpur Sahib Resolution and Sikh dignity, martyred in 1984.
Epitome of selfless compassion and founder of All India Pingalwara Society in Amritsar; a pioneer of environmental conservation who devoted his entire life to caring for the disabled and destitute.
Devout saint who established Gurdwara Sachkhand Langar Sahib at Takht Sri Hazur Sahib in Nanded, dedicating his life to continuous 24-hour Langar service for all pilgrims.
Heroic commander of 21 brave soldiers of the 36th Sikhs who defended Saragarhi military post against 10,000 Afghan tribesmen on September 12, 1897, fighting to the last breath.

persons.nameGurmukhi: ਮਾਰਸ਼ਲ ਆਫ਼ ਦਾ ਏਅਰ ਫ਼ੋਰਸ ਅਰਜਨ ਸਿੰਘ
persons.nameRoman: Marshal of the IAF Arjan Singh
persons.nameHindi: मार्शल ऑफ द एयर फोर्स अर्जन सिंह
persons.shortBio: Legendary aviator and the only five-star rank officer in Indian Air Force history, who brilliantly led the IAF through the 1965 Indo-Pak War with fearless leadership and poise.

persons.nameRoman: Flying Officer Nirmal Jit Singh Sekhon
persons.shortBio: The only Indian Air Force officer awarded the Param Vir Chakra (India's highest wartime gallantry award), who single-handedly defended Srinagar airfield against 6 PAF Sabre jets in 1971.
Param Vir Chakra recipient who commanded a platoon of 1 Sikh at Tongpen La near Bum La in the 1962 Sino-Indian War, holding off three consecutive waves of Chinese assaults against impossible odds.
General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Eastern Command who planned and led the historic 13-day liberation of Bangladesh in the 1971 war, accepting the surrender of 93,000 Pakistani troops in Dhaka.
Master of guerrilla warfare who trained the Mukti Bahini fighters during the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War and later served as a revered military strategist for the Panth in 1984.
Fearless human rights defender who uncovered the illegal cremations of over 25,000 disappeared youths in Punjab, speaking to international parliaments and attaining martyrdom for truth in 1995.
Historic trailblazer who became the first Sikh, first Indian American, and first Asian American ever elected to the United States Congress, serving three terms from 1957 to 1963.
Pioneering Canadian politician who served as the 33rd Premier of British Columbia (first person of Asian origin to lead a Canadian province) and later as Canada's Federal Minister of Health.
The 'Peach King of California', visionary farmer, and philanthropist who became the largest peach grower in the world and supported Sikh cultural and religious institutions across the diaspora.
The 'Turbaned Tornado', centenarian British-Sikh marathon runner who completed full 42 km marathons at age 100+, carrying the Olympic Torch in London 2012 and inspiring millions globally.

World-renowned physicist celebrated internationally as the 'Father of Fiber Optics', whose groundbreaking discoveries revolutionized high-speed communications, biomedical lasers, and internet technology.
Pioneering cosmic ray physicist, researcher on the Manhattan Project with Arthur Compton, and fellow of the American Physical Society who advised Pandit Nehru on atomic energy research.
Monumental Sikh scholar and lexicographer who authored the 4-volume encyclopedia 'Mahan Kosh' (Gur Shabad Ratnakar Mahan Kosh) and the seminal treatise 'Ham Hindu Nahin'.
Master grammarian and scholar who decoded Gurbani Viyakaran (Sikh scripture grammar) and authored the monumental 10-volume 'Sri Guru Granth Sahib Darpan', an unparalleled exegesis.
Revered as the 'Father of Modern Punjabi Literature', poet, scholar, and theologian honored with the Padma Bhushan and Sahitya Akademi Award, author of Sundari, Bijay Singh, and Rana Surat Singh.
Doyen of Punjab and Sikh historiography, founder of the Punjab History Conference, prolific researcher who authored definitive historical works on Banda Singh Bahadur and Ahmad Shah Durrani.
Celebrated author, historian, and journalist who authored the definitive two-volume scholarly work 'A History of the Sikhs' and iconic historical novels including 'Train to Pakistan'.
'The Flying Sikh', legendary track and field Olympian, four-time Asian Games gold medalist, and Commonwealth Games champion who put Sikh athletics onto the global world stage.
